newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's militant unionists clash with police.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's militant unionists clash with police.

text.p: Anti-government protests over a controversial labour law rang in the New Year in South Korea, and unionists threatened new strikes once the holiday is over.
About 5,000 South Korean militant unionists clashed with riot police on Tuesday night when they took to the streets protesting the law, which they see as a threat to their job security.
"Police fired teargas when protesters tried to pour out into the Seoul streets from Myungdong Cathedral where they had been staging a sit-in protest," a witness said. No injuries were reported.
Protesters later joined crowds gathered in Seoul to mark the beginning of the New Year. Waving banners, they chanted: "Down with the Kim Young-sam government."

Workers launched strikes on December 26 after the ruling New Korea Party rammed a new labour law through parliament that gives employers the right to lay off workers, hire temporary workers and replace strikers.
Strikes were called off for the New Year holidays, but union leaders threatened further action after the holidays to back their demands for the new law to be withdrawn.

The nation's largest umbrella union group, the Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU), said it would launch strikes again immediately "if the government and employers try to resolve the issue with force".
The outlawed Korea Confederation of Trade Unions (KCTU) said on Tuesday it would ask unions at automakers, shipyards, metal workers and manufacturers to walk out again on Friday.

Union employees at hospitals, the Hyundai Group, construction and chemical firms and white-collar workers will join them on January 6. On January 7, subway and broadcast unions are set to strike, the KCTU said.

The two umbrella union groups claim an aggregate 1.7 million members in most of South Korea's major industries, including auto manufacturing, shipbuilding, and public sector services such as subways and hospitals. The FKTU said its second round of strikes would be led by unions in the public and service sectors.
